header:
Date: 2027-04-07
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (BrightScale Head of ML), Jamal Owens (BrightScale Platform Eng), Eli Park (BrightScale SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput results and tuning progress. Discussed continuous batching tweaks, concurrency targets, queue headroom, and tradeoffs for latency vs cost. Agreed on microbenchmark with higher concurrency and to share updated pricing for dedicated slot options.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, um we're on for 45 minutes. Quick agenda - status, bench results, tuning, next steps.
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: Yep thanks Alex. We saw the baseline run you sent last week, p50 looked fine but p95 still high under load, so we're hoping the batching changes help.
[00:35] Priya Kapoor: Right, so recap - last run we enabled continuous batching at 64 token window and set batch target to 16 requests. We also adjusted the kv cache prewarm but the billing reported a slight increase because of longer in-flight contexts, that might be a config issue.
[00:54] Jamal Owens: A quick note - our production traffic is pretty spiky, bursts up to 800 rps for short periods. We expect concurrency peaks that blow past the pilot baseline.
[01:12] Eli Park: And SRE wants to avoid long queueing, so we need clear queue headroom numbers before we move to dedicated.
[01:28] Alex Chen: Totally. Priya, can you walk through the recent microbenchmark numbers? I pulled the spreadsheet but some columns looked swapped.
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: Yeah sure. So the run labeled '0304-cont-batch' - with concurrency 8 we got 1.2k tokens/sec, p50 85ms per token, p95 420ms. When we increased to concurrency 16 throughput rose to 2.0k tokens/sec but p95 jumped to 720ms. There's a sweet spot around 12 where latency and throughput balance.
[02:05] Marta Ruiz: That sounds like the classic latency vs batching tradeoff. Do we have metrics on queue depth and time-in-queue?
[02:15] Priya Kapoor: We logged queue depth - at conc 16 the average queue was 40ms but tail hit 350ms which contributes to p95. Also noticed KV cache hit rate dropped marginally when we pushed concurrency since locks for cache warming contended. Might be a mis-typed cache key or race in prewarm.
[02:36] Jamal Owens: Could that be the KV cash/key thing you mentioned earlier? Sometimes the transcript from the last run said 'KV cash' which confused us heh.
[02:46] Priya Kapoor: Yeah sorry, kv cache - the infra writes were contending. We can avoid by staggering prewarm or using per-worker warming.
[02:56] Alex Chen: Also to surface one more variable - model choice. You're on a quantized 13B variant; we tested a 7B and saw lower latency but quality drop on safety prompts. Any flexibility there?
[03:12] Marta Ruiz: We need the 13B quality for our customer-facing summaries. So preference is keep model but tune serving.
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: Ok understood. For the POC we recommend two parallel paths: 1) Tune batching/concurrency and measure p95/p99 with realistic traffic; 2) Try small routing rule to offload tail traffic to a cheaper lower-latency rack or lower precision variant as fallback. Both are doable.
[03:41] Eli Park: For #2 how would fallback affect cost and correctness? We cannot surface hallucinated lower-quality answers.
[03:50] Priya Kapoor: Fallback would be a degenerate response or a rate-limited 7B only for non-critical paths, or we could return a cached prefix; we'd need your acceptance criteria.
[04:01] Alex Chen: Quick question Marta - what's your SLO target? p95 under 500ms? p99 under 1.5s?
[04:10] Marta Ruiz: Ideally p95 < 500ms, p99 < 2s. If we can get p95 < 400ms even better but we know that is tight.
[04:19] Priya Kapoor: Great we'll aim for p95 < 500ms. Next, the microbenchmark plan - Priya: describe the new run.
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: For the next run we'll bump concurrency to 24 but with dynamic batching thresholding: reduce max batch size to 12, and enable per-request early flush if queue time > 120ms. Also will run a variant with 4x concurrency but smaller batch target to see sweet spot. We'll capture token throughput, request latency, queue time, and KV hit rates.
[04:50] Jamal Owens: Ok that aligns with our traffic; we especially want to see behavior during 2-minute spikes.
[04:58] Alex Chen: And we'll run a simulated spike pattern too, right?
[05:02] Priya Kapoor: Yes - Priya: we'll run both steady-state and spike sim; I'll attach the scripts.
[05:09] Marta Ruiz: Please also export the raw logs and the per-worker metrics; last time we got aggregate only and couldn't pinpoint contention.
[05:16] Priya Kapoor: Got it, raw per-worker logs plus tracing spans. Might be a lot of data but we'll compress.
[05:22] Alex Chen: On the infra side, a few quick options - Dedicated GPU pool would give you more predictable throughput, or Reserved slots with scaling headroom. I'll share pricing.
[05:33] Marta Ruiz: Is dedicated necessary if we tune batching? We prefer not to commit until we see steady metrics.
[05:40] Alex Chen: Totally reasonable. The pilot's goal is to show you can meet SLOs without heavy commitment; if pilot shows variance we can propose a reserved capacity with auto-burst.
[05:50] Eli Park: From SRE side, we also need logging and audit for private deployment if we go that route - SSO, KMS, and SOC2 papers.
[05:59] Alex Chen: We'll include our SOC 2 and ISO docs; for KMS we integrate with your cloud KMS or HSM options in Redwood Private. I'll send the security packet.
[06:10] Marta Ruiz: That would be great. Also curious about autoscaler queue behavior - when you autoscale, how does batching adapt? We saw some jitter last time.
[06:20] Priya Kapoor: Good question. Our autoscaler considers both cpu/gpu utilization and queue latency; when we spin up a worker there is a warm-up period for kv cache which can temporarily increase tail latency. We mitigated by prewarming and staggered join. For pilot we can enable staggered join to reduce jitter.
[06:38] Jamal Owens: Can you quantify the warm-up penalty?
[06:41] Priya Kapoor: In tests, a new worker took ~6-12s to prewarm KV cache for common prefixes; during that window p95 rose by about 20-30%. Staggered join reduces concurrent warms and keeps overall p95 stable.
[06:57] Marta Ruiz: Ok noted. On the queueing policy - do you support priority queues by route? We have real-time scoring vs async summarization.
[07:08] Priya Kapoor: Yes you can set per-route priorities and token-level budgets. For the POC we recommend isolating real-time routes into a higher priority pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[07:20] Alex Chen: We'll draft a recommended config: dedicated priority pool for scoring (low-latency), separate pool for batchy summarization with larger batches.
[07:29] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. Also any quick wins on quantization or kernel selection?
[07:34] Priya Kapoor: We already used int8 quantization for the 13B. Next step is kernel tuning for sequence-length distribution; your average prompt length is 120 tokens, but some sequences spike to 800 - we can optimize for the 120 path and handle long ones separately, that reduces average path cost.
[07:53] Eli Park: That makes sense. We'll upload the prompt length histogram today.
[07:58] Alex Chen: Great. Anything on security/compliance we should follow up on now?
[08:03] Marta Ruiz: Please send SOC2, encryption docs, and the network diagram for Redwood Private. We'll need to loop Legal if we consider Private.
[08:12] Alex Chen: Will do. Priya, any anomalies in logs from last run worth calling out?
[08:17] Priya Kapoor: Two things - transient OOM on worker 3 at high concurrency (we traced to batching + long context length); and weird header parsing for some client requests causing retries. We recommend a client-side guardrail on prompt length and retry backoff.
[08:32] Jamal Owens: We'll add a server-side reject if prompt > 2,000 tokens to avoid OOM.
[08:37] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. For the microbenchmark I'll include a variant that caps prompt lengths to reproduce.
[08:44] Marta Ruiz: Timeline-wise, can we expect updated numbers by next Tuesday?
[08:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes, I'll run them over the weekend and share Monday/Tue.
[08:52] Alex Chen: And Alex will send pricing by Friday.
[08:55] Alex Chen: Yep. Anything else?
[08:58] Eli Park: One last ask - can you add p99 traces for the next run? That helps root cause tails.
[09:05] Priya Kapoor: Will do - include p99 histograms and traces.
[09:10] Alex Chen: Ok recap - Priya runs 4x concurrency microbench and spike sim, Marta uploads traffic sample, Alex shares pricing and security docs. We'll meet same time next week unless we need a deep-dive earlier.
[09:25] Marta Ruiz: Thanks all.
[09:27] Jamal Owens: Thanks.
[09:30] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript contains some auto-transcription errors (KV cache spelled cash, occasional speaker mismatch). Links referenced: pilot results spreadsheet (https://redwood.internal/pilots/brightscale-results.xlsx), pilot-deck (https://redwood.in/pilot-deck), security packet (https://redwood.in/security-packet).
